title: Level 5 (World Class) - B-20
notes:
West leads the ♣K against 7♠. West's opening club lead is won by the ♣A. South's best chance is to set up the dummy. A club should, therefore, be ruffed at trick 2.

South crosses to dummy in trumps and leads another club. When East ruffs in, South must overruff and reconsider. If hearts break 3-3, South will have to hope that the remaining spades are 1-1 so that he will be able to ruff his diamond loser in the dummy.

If hearts are not breaking, South needs some kind of squeeze. East is likely to have length in hearts (due to West's club length) and a double squeeze may be possible with diamonds as the suit guarded by both defenders.

South should begin by drawing another round of trump to which both defenders follow. Another club can now be ruffed in the closed hand. South can cash 3 rounds of hearts, noting East's length in the suit. A diamond is played to the dummy and North's last spade will squeeze both defenders.

East must keep his heart as a guard to South's ♥2. East thus pitches a diamond, transferring the sole defensive guard to the West hand. South pitches the ♥2 and West is now squeezed. A club discard will set up North's last club. West must also pitch a diamond and South will take the last 2 tricks in diamonds.

Double squeezes mature with 1 loser. South starts with 2 losers (1 in diamonds and 1 in hearts), but the dummy reversal technique of ruffing 3 clubs in the South hand increases South's trick count to 12. The double squeeze produces trick 13.

In every double squeeze, both defenders are squeezed in a common suit (diamonds in this hand). That suit must contain an entry. Each defender is also solely responsible for guarding another suit (East guards hearts, West guards clubs).

Several forms of double squeeze exist. Depending on the nature of the winners and entries in the threat suits, a double squeeze may not function or it may be difficult to play in the ending. The above position is fairly straight forward. South must be careful, however, to cash his top hearts before playing North's last trump.
